# Nanook

> Nanook is an open-source toolkit for defining test cases in XLSX spreadsheets (equivalence class, matrix and specification tables) and generating test data through pluggable generators and writers. Written in TypeScript, shipped as one ESM package with type declarations, requires Node.js >= 22. Current release: @xhubio/nanook-table 3.3.1 (2026-10-03).

The docs pages below (Documentation except the hub, Tutorials, and the 3.x API reference; not the 1.x API pages) are also available as Markdown: append `.md` to the URL (for example https://nanook.xhub.io/docs/quickstart/quickstart.md). The whole documentation in one file: https://nanook.xhub.io/llms-full.txt. The npm package ships the 3.x docs as Markdown in node_modules/@xhubio/nanook-table/docs/.

## Documentation
- [agents.md](https://nanook.xhub.io/agents.md): One guide a coding agent follows end to end to add Nanook test cases and test data to a project: install, which skill to read, what goes in a cell, how to check the count
- [Documentation Hub](https://nanook.xhub.io/docs): Entry page linking quickstart, guide, tutorials, modules, and API reference
- [Quickstart Guide](https://nanook.xhub.io/docs/quickstart/quickstart): Introduction to creating an equivalence class table and generating test data from it
- [Quickstart with Claude Code](https://nanook.xhub.io/docs/quickstart/claude-code): Install the skill as a Claude Code plugin, let Claude Code draft the decision table, generate the data with Nanook
- [Use with AI agents](https://nanook.xhub.io/docs/guide/use-with-ai): The skills, a rules block for AGENTS.md, and the docs as plain text for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot and other agents
- [General Overview](https://nanook.xhub.io/docs/guide/generalOverview): Architecture and concepts of Nanook Table
- [Equivalence Class Tables](https://nanook.xhub.io/docs/guide/equivalence/overview): How to define test cases using equivalence classes
- [Matrix Tables](https://nanook.xhub.io/docs/guide/matrix/overview): Pairwise or combinatorial relationships between two dimensions of test parameters
- [Data Generators](https://nanook.xhub.io/docs/guide/generatrorCommand/generator): Generator directives and custom generator functions
- [Static Data](https://nanook.xhub.io/docs/guide/generatrorCommand/static): Static test data definitions
- [References](https://nanook.xhub.io/docs/guide/generatrorCommand/reference): Cross-table data references
- [Instance IDs](https://nanook.xhub.io/docs/guide/advanced/instanceIds): How repeated generator calls produce one coherent record
- [Current 3.x documentation in the repository](https://github.com/xhubio/nanook-table/tree/master/docs): Guides (decision, matrix and specification tables, directives), tutorials and API reference for the TypeScript version. The 1.x API pages on this site carry a version note; the 3.x reference is under /docs/api/v3/.

## API Reference (1.x, historical)
- [API Hub](https://nanook.xhub.io/docs/api): Entry page listing all eight module groups of the 1.x API reference

- [Data Generator Base](https://nanook.xhub.io/docs/api/dataGenerator/DataGeneratorBase): Base class for generators (the registry is TDGServiceRegistry in 1.x, DataGeneratorRegistry in 3.x)
- [Table Decision](https://nanook.xhub.io/docs/api/model-decision/TableDecision): Decision table model
- [File Processor](https://nanook.xhub.io/docs/api/file-processor/FileProcessor): Spreadsheet file handling
- [3.x API reference — Processor](https://nanook.xhub.io/docs/api/v3/processor): TestcaseProcessor, writers, filters, factory functions (generated from the repository)
- [3.x API reference — Model](https://nanook.xhub.io/docs/api/v3/model): Table and test case interfaces, directive types
- [3.x API reference — Data generator](https://nanook.xhub.io/docs/api/v3/data-generator): DataGeneratorBase, DataGeneratorRegistry, GeneratorFaker
- [3.x API reference — File processor](https://nanook.xhub.io/docs/api/v3/file-processor): Importers, parsers, specification converter
- [3.x API reference — Logger](https://nanook.xhub.io/docs/api/v3/logger): LoggerInterface, LoggerMemory
- [3.x API reference source](https://github.com/xhubio/nanook-table/tree/master/docs/api): the Markdown these five pages are generated from

## Key Facts
- Open source, MIT license (GitHub: https://github.com/xhubio/nanook-table; npm: @xhubio/nanook-table, current release 3.3.1, 2026-10-03)
- Written in TypeScript; one ESM package with type declarations; requires Node.js >= 22
- Reads XLSX files (.xlsx and .xls via the built-in importer); other formats need a custom importer
- Table types: <DECISION_TABLE> (equivalence class table), <MATRIX_TABLE>, <SPECIFICATION_TABLE> (also <SPECIFICATION>; field rules converted into a decision table)
- Cell directives: gen:<instanceId>:<generator>:<parameter> calls a generator, ref: references a value from another test case, plain cells are static values
- Built-in Faker generator (@faker-js/faker); custom generators extend DataGeneratorBase
- Writes one JSON file per test case by default; any other format (CSV, database, API) through a custom writer
- Tag-based filters select which test cases are processed
- Claude Code skill create-equivalence-class-table (since 2.1.0; in English, ships as a plugin from the GitHub repository, listed on skills.sh and Context7): plugin via /plugin marketplace add xhubio/nanook-table and /plugin install nanook@nanook (invoked as /nanook:create-equivalence-class-table); for other agents npx skills add xhubio/nanook-table --skill create-equivalence-class-table; also in the npm package under skills/ (versions after 3.0.1), the slash command /createEquivalenceClassTable under .claude/commands/
- Claude Code skill generate-test-data (since 3.2.0, same plugin): starts from an existing workbook, checks it with inspect-workbook.mts (minimum test case count, unregistered generators, broken references), writes missing generators, generates one JSON per test case and wires the fixtures into Vitest or Playwright tests; invoked as /nanook:generate-test-data, for other agents npx skills add xhubio/nanook-table --skill generate-test-data
- A rules block for a project's AGENTS.md (Codex, Cursor, Copilot; Claude Code via @AGENTS.md in CLAUDE.md) is on https://nanook.xhub.io/docs/guide/use-with-ai; there is no Nanook MCP server yet
- Used by Deutsche Bahn and other enterprises
- Published by BeeBack UG (haftungsbeschränkt), xhub.io
